items.prompt: Why can a default parameter tags=[] retain values across separate calls?

options.text: Python creates that default object when defining the function
options.why: The default object can then be reused by later calls.

options.text: Python creates an empty replacement list at every call
options.why: That would avoid retention, but is not how this default works.

options.text: All local lists are automatically global variables
options.why: Local lists can be new per call; the default is a separate issue.

options.text: Lists cannot be changed after a function returns
options.why: A list remains mutable while references to it exist.

items.explanation: A mutable default is one object created at definition time. Using None and allocating inside the function avoids accidental sharing for omitted arguments.
